rows.name: synchronous and asynchronous telemetry failures never interfere with successful inference

assertions.native_check: Exact original observable predicate with the original five-event factory sequence and actual supported returned-future rejection handling, both rejected outcomes proven before joined owner shutdown.
assertions.api_adaptation: The original status callback factory increments synchronously, throws on odd invocations and returns a rejected Promise on even invocations. The true native EventSink wrapper executes each admitted factory synchronously, preserves the five event order/count, contains all three actual factory panics and independently polls both actual returned Err futures on its one bounded owned worker. No detached failing task is substituted for a returned result. Source rejections carry JavaScript Error messages. Native returned futures use payload-free ObserverRejected; private rejection strings are intentionally outside this typed API. Actual factory panic message Status storage unavailable remains synthetic test input. Routine safe logs/statuses exclude it and the source asynchronous error string. Global panic hooks are not mutated in ordinary parallel tests; root host/subprocess privacy evidence qualifies stderr separately.

comparison_boundaries: Additive replay of the complete frozen original #26 callback captured earlier with all three successful source assertions and the exact five status callback invocations. The prior partial native test/report remain byte-identical; their missing async-return precondition is now exercised through a separate supported native adapter rather than rewritten as past coverage.

The original status callback factory increments synchronously, throws on odd invocations and returns a rejected Promise on even invocations. The true native EventSink wrapper executes each admitted factory synchronously, preserves the five event order/count, contains all three actual factory panics and independently polls both actual returned Err futures on its one bounded owned worker. No detached failing task is substituted for a returned result.

Source rejections carry JavaScript Error messages. Native returned futures use payload-free ObserverRejected; private rejection strings are intentionally outside this typed API. Actual factory panic message Status storage unavailable remains synthetic test input. Routine safe logs/statuses exclude it and the source asynchronous error string. Global panic hooks are not mutated in ordinary parallel tests; root host/subprocess privacy evidence qualifies stderr separately.

Default observer pending timeout is disabled. Both actual returned rejections are observed after completed HTTP inference and before owner close; numeric before-close rejected=2/factory_panicked=3/pending=0/charged_bytes=0/cancelled=0 controls prevent owner shutdown from manufacturing the rejected outcomes. Explicit bounded close joins the worker and retains identical counters, with worker_finished=true.

The source fixture supplied routing callback remains supplied in native code, preserving its exact captured Haiku decision and complete request document. No live evaluator calls occur. Real provider/client loopback HTTP retains every delivered byte, actual response headers and all semantic forwarding/authentication headers.

Generated UUID and measured first_response_ms/total_latency_ms differ between runs and remain raw. Native controls correlate every actual event/route/completion ID and validate timing presence/nonnegative values. Source undefined event fields become absent native fields; optional typed RouteOptions identifiers use empty strings. Actual numeric values compare as JavaScript Number values without rewriting raw metadata.

Source mocked complete is called twice for successful cleanup and returns undefined. Native Gateway consumes its request lease once and the supplied mock returns false. All actual source/native callbacks remain raw; the body has a model observation but no stop reason or confirmed completion evidence. Callback cardinality equality or production continuation acceptance is not claimed.

Passive source capture preserves the provider callback unread request stream. Native bounded peer reads the complete finite synthetic request before responding. Full body/header policy parity is checked; unread-stream API/timing equivalence is not asserted.
